problem.paragraph: Find the volume of the solid of revolution obtained by revolving the region bounded by the graphs of $$f(x) = 5 - x^{2}$$ and $$g(x) = 1$$ about the $$x$$ -axis.

solution.paragraph: To find the points of intersection of the two curves, we solve the equation $$5 - x^{2} = 1$$ , giving $$x = \pm 2$$ (see the figure). Using Formula (19), we find the required volume:

image.alt: Details A downward opening parabola is plotted in the x y coordinate plane. The horizontal axis x, ranges from negative 3 to over positive 3 with a rotational arrow around it and the vertical axis y ranges from 0 to over 5. The parabola labeled f (x) = 5 minus x^2 is symmetric about the vertical axis such that it enters the third quadrant in the bottom left corner of the viewing window, passes through the horizontal axis around (negative 2.1, 0) to enter the second quadrant, then slopes upward gradually to the right, cuts vertical axis on which its vertex rests at (0, 5), and turns downward to enter the first quadrant, slopes downward gradually to the right, passes through the horizontal axis around (2.1, 0) and exits at the bottom right corner of the viewing window. A horizontal line labeled g (x) = 1 runs through the y coordinate (0, 1) above the x axis. The region bound by the parabola and the horizontal line, is shaded.

exercises.instruction: In Exercises 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14, find the volume of the solid obtained by revolving the region under the curve $$y = f(x)$$ from $$x = a$$ to $$x = b$$ about the $$x$$ -axis.

In Exercises 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 and 22, find the volume of the solid obtained by revolving the region bounded above by the curve $$y = f(x)$$ and below by the curve $$y = g(x)$$ from $$x = a$$ to $$x = b$$ about the $$x$$ -axis.
In Exercises 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29 and 30, find the volume of the solid obtained by revolving the region bounded by the graphs of the functions about the $$x$$ -axis.

problem.paragraph: Hint: You will need to evaluate two integrals.

By computing the volume of the solid obtained by revolving the region under the semicircle $$y = \sqrt{r^{2} - x^{2}}$$ from $$x = - r$$ to $$x = r$$ about the $$x$$ -axis, show that the volume of a sphere of radius $$r$$ is $$\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$$ cubic units.

Volume of a Football Find the volume of the prolate spheroid (a solid of revolution in the shape of a football) obtained by revolving the region under the graph of the function $$y = \frac{3}{5}\sqrt{25 - x^{2}}$$ from $$x = - 5$$ to $$x = 5$$ about the $$x$$ -axis.
